ProgramName: Master of Arts in Applied Sociology
Requirements: Graduate Degree-Seeking Application, including:* Residency Form Goal Statement Official Transcript, showing:* Conferral of Bachelor's degree* Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Writing Sample From coursework in sociology or a related discipline. Applicants can submit any course paper, thesis, or capstone project that best represents their skills in research and writing. Resume Two (2) Letters of Recommendation.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The Master of Arts in Applied Sociology at UMBC is a qualitative-focused graduate program where students learn the interplay of core theories, methods, research, and service in the social sciences. The program emphasizes the 'practical side' of sociology and the acquisition of analytical skills for employment in various professional settings, including public and private organizations involved in social research, policy, and program development. [7, 8] It is designed to help sociologists advance their careers and professional skills, with a focus on methodology and statistics across topics like health, medicine, aging, diversity, equity and inclusion, and applied research methods. [8] Students are prepared to become 'embedded sociologists' who conduct change-oriented research in communities or organizations. [13]
Accredidation: University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) is an accredited institution and a member of the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [12] The university's accreditation was reaffirmed on March 2, 2017. [12] No specific accreditation for the Master of Arts in Applied Sociology program is mentioned on the university's accreditation page. [12]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education
Requirements: The Master of Arts in Education (MAE) is a 36-credit, 12-course program for educators who already have teaching experience and hold a teaching certificate. [5, 16] It is designed to help experienced teachers prepare for roles in educational and curricular leadership, curriculum development, and in-service teacher professional development. [10] Applicants are expected to have an undergraduate degree with a GPA of 3.0 or higher, a teaching certificate, and provide three professional or academic references. [11] A statement of purpose/goals is also required. [11]
Concentration.1: Early Childhood Education, Elementary Education, Reading/Literacy, Secondary Education, Mathematics Education, Science Education, Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Description: The Master of Arts in Education is a degree program for educators who wish to enhance their career through advanced professional knowledge. This program does not lead to initial teacher certification. UMBC’s Master of Arts in Education (M.A.Ed.) is designed to meet the needs of teachers and other professionals in education. The program is committed to preparing educators for a variety of roles in an ever-changing, diverse, and technologically complex world. At the heart of our work is a commitment to social justice and a dedication to meeting the needs of all learners.
Accredidation: The Master of Arts in Education programs are not CAEP accredited.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education with a concentration in STEM Education
Requirements:
In addition to the general university requirements for admission to the Graduate School, the following are required:

*   A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
*   Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions are to be sent to the Graduate School.
*   A completed application including a resume, a statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s goals and three letters of recommendation.
*   Standardized tests (e.g., GRE) are not required for an application to be considered complete.
Department: Department of Education
Concentration.1: STEM Education
Description: The Master of Arts in Education (M.A.E.) is a graduate program for certified teachers or other educators who are interested in expanding their content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and leadership skills. The program is designed for educators who are committed to their own professional growth and the mentoring of other teaching professionals. With the program’s emphasis on teacher leadership, the program is ideal for those who aspire to become leading teachers in their content area. The M.A.E. program combines the study of education and the academic disciplines of mathematics, science or STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics). Through UMBC’s partnerships with local school systems, M.A.E. cohort programs can be customized to meet the needs of a participating school district.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Historical Studies
Requirements:
The process of strengthening your graduate school application starts while you are still an undergraduate. Here is a timeline and suggestions for avenues to explore while you are pursuing your undergraduate degree.

Freshman and sophomore years. Assess your interests, abilities, and career goals; Identify a mentor; Look into graduate school preparation events (e.g., boot camps, pre-application campus visits, summer programs).

Junior year. Gather information on graduate programs; Gather application materials; Learn about entrance examination requirements and dates; Investigate application deadlines.

Pre-Senior Summer. Narrow your list of graduate schools; Investigate funding sources; Write the first draft of your statement of purpose; Contact recommendation sources.

Senior year (Start Early). Select the schools you want to apply to; Register for entrance exams; Submit completed applications. [1]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Intercultural Communication
Requirements:
Applicants seeking admission to the MAICC should have a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field with a strong academic record (minimum 3.0 GPA out of 4) from a recognized university. Applicants are required to submit an IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 79 in order to demonstrate their proficiency in English. Applicants can be exempt from this requirement if they meet one of the conditions listed below:.

Academic transcripts. [1]

Official electronic copies of transcripts should be submitted as part of the online application. [1]
Final transcripts and graduation statements are required for all previous university studies. [1]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The Department of Modern Languages, Linguistics and Intercultural Communication (MLLI) offers a program leading to an M.A. in Intercultural Communication. This program provides a core of theory and research in the fields of linguistics and intercultural communication, combined with a related block of courses in one of three concentrations: applied linguistics and second language acquisition research, intercultural training in public and private sector contexts or for specific purposes (e.g., modern language or English-as-a-second-language instruction, translation/interpreting) or cultural studies (e.g., analysis of French and Francophone, Hispanic, German, or Russian cultures).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Learning and Performance Technology
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in any subject and 3.0 GPA or above on a 4.0 scale. [3]
Department: Division of Professional Studies
Description: The Master of Arts in Learning and Performance Technology is a graduate program offered by the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). [1] This program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to design, deliver, support, and measure training, learning, and performance within organizations. [1] Learning and Performance Technology (LAPT), formerly named ISD, is one of UMBC's most established graduate programs. [4] Our online certificates and master's programs provide an innovative and career-focused curriculum. [4] We offer all courses in an online format to accommodate the schedules of busy working professionals. [4] If you are interested in solving problems in organizations by designing, delivering, supporting, and measuring training, learning, and performance within organizations, the LAPT graduate program at UMBC will prepare you to do exactly that. [4] The Master of Arts in Learning and Performance Technology (previously ISD) requires a minimum of 36 credits hours. [2] Students must complete seven required core courses (totaling 21 credits), five elective courses (totaling 15 credits) and complete a professional portfolio. [2]
ScholarshipType: UMBC participates in all federal and state student financial aid programs and offers scholarships and assistantships through the Graduate School, Graduate Departments and the Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships. [19]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Management of Aging Services
Requirements: The graduate programs at the Erickson School of Aging Studies provide integrated, interdisciplinary professional training for leaders in the growing longevity economy. Graduates will meet a growing workforce need for leaders with professional education to serve in management positions in public, private, and non-profit/advocacy organizations providing services to older adults. [8]
Department: UMBC Erickson School of Aging Studies
Description:
The curriculum consists of a blend of core courses which draw from and integrate our three focal areas, inclusive of their history, theory, current knowledge base and fundamental analytic/practice skills. Upon completion of the requirements for the proposed degree, the student will be able to: 

*   Exercise a holistic set of skills and knowledge that integrates management, policy, and aging.
*   Apply core management fundamentals of strategy, marketing, operations, finance and accounting to aging services organizations across the private, public and non-profit sectors.
*   Demonstrate a knowledge of normal human aging on the individual level, including social, psychological and physical aspects.
*   More effectively provide leadership to their organizations and manage other individuals.
*   Understand the societal implications of an aging population for public policy, the economy and major social institutions.
*   Evaluate a broad range of organizational outcomes utilizing research, policy and business criteria for performance.
*   Effectively apply critical thinking, effective communication and creative problem solving to their organizations.
*   Describe in detail the existing array of public sector aging services programs, the role of policy in shaping their future roles and impacts, and the emergent private sector organizations developing desired services for this population.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching
Requirements: Applicants must be accepted and admitted to the UMBC Graduate School and the UMBC Department of Education. Minimum admission requirements include an undergraduate GPA of 2.75 for admission and 3.0 for internship. [7] The first step in the application process is to schedule a personal interview with an advisor of the program and submit transcripts of all prior undergraduate and graduate study for analysis. [7, 8]
Department: Department of Education

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Requirements:
In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, the following are required for the M.A. in TESOL program:


	* A bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
	* A statement of purpose (500 words).
	* A summary of the applicant’s experience learning and/or teaching languages (This can be part of the statement of purpose or a separate C.V./resume.)
	* Three letters of recommendation.
	* For non-native speakers of English, a minimum TOEFL score of 96 (with a minimum of 23 on the combined listening and speaking sections and 22 on the reading and writing sections) on the internet-based test (iBT). As an alternative to the TOEFL, we also accept the International English Language Testing System (IELTS). The minimum acceptable score is 7.0, with a minimum of 6.5 on all sections (Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking).


Official GRE scores are not required for admission.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Texts, Technologies, and Literature
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited university. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is required. The application also requires three letters of recommendation and a sample of critical writing (15-20 pages).
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: Provides students with the opportunity for advanced study of texts, technologies, and literature. Students will explore a range of literatures in English and a variety of textual forms, media and practices in relation to their cultural contexts. They will also develop advanced skills in reading, analyzing and writing about texts, from the lyric poem to digital work in multimedia. Additionally, students will have the opportunity to study language in use in various settings, or to specialize in the study of communication or the teaching of composition.

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Biotechnology
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in science, engineering, or any subject with sufficient coursework in relevant life science topics such as foundations of biology and organic chemistry OR a bachelor's degree in any subject combined with work experience in the life sciences. [2] A 3.0 GPA or above on a 4.0 scale is also required. [2]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences, Division of Professional Studies
Description: UMBC's biotechnology master's degree is designed to provide students with the skills sought by the biotechnology industry. The curriculum offers advanced instruction in the life sciences, along with coursework in regulatory affairs, leadership, management, commercialization and legal issues inherent to a life science-oriented business.

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Community Leadership
Requirements:
To be considered for regular admission to the Graduate School, a prospective student must:

- Submit a non-refundable application fee.
- Have a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university, or from a foreign university or college with a degree recognized as equivalent to a U.S. bachelor’s degree.
- Have a minimum undergraduate grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Applicants with GPAs below 3.0 may be considered for provisional admission.
- Submit an official transcript from each college or university attended. All transcripts must be in English.
- Provide a statement of academic goals and research interests. [1]
- Three letters of recommendation are required for all graduate degrees. [1]
Department: UMBC Professional Studies
Description: The UMBC community leadership programs envision learning and working together to champion vibrant communities. The community leadership program’s mission is to build communities inside and outside the classroom that are rooted in relationships and brought to life through co-teaching, co-learning, and co-creating. The program aims to lead institutional change in higher education toward a core institutional identity as citizens in our greater Baltimore community.

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Data Science
Requirements:
In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, the following are required for the program:

A bachelor’s degree in a STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) field is preferred.
A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Completed application, statement of goals, resume and official transcripts.
GRE scores are not required. [1]
Department: The Graduate School
Concentration.1: The Data Science program has two tracks: Data Science Track and Analytics Track.
Description: The Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Data Science is an exciting graduate program that prepares students from a wide range of disciplinary backgrounds for careers in data science. In the core courses, students will get a fundamental understanding of data science through classes that highlight machine learning, data analysis and data management. The core courses will also introduce students to ethical and legal implications surrounding data science. Beyond the core courses, students will take three courses in domain specific pathways developed in collaboration with academic departments across the university. Through these pathways, students will apply the skills and techniques they learned in the core courses to their own field or area of expertise. Upon graduation, students will be prepared for a career in the field of data science.

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Entrepreneurship, Innovation, and Leadership
Description: With three pathways in entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, and socialpreneurship, you can tailor your education to your interests and career goals. Whether you are looking to start your own company, drive social change through innovation, or incorporate innovative practices into your current workplace, UMBC’s Master of Professional Studies (MPS) in Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Leadership is the ideal program to help you meet your goals. [1] Designed for working professionals in both small and large organizations, the program equips students with entrepreneurial thinking skills that prepare them to become drivers of change in both the workplace and in their communities. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Geographic Information Systems
Requirements:
In addition to a completed application, the following information is required:

- A bachelor’s degree in any field is required.
- A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required for admission. 
- Official transcripts from all colleges/universities attended.
- A current resume.
- A statement of goals and academic/professional experience.

GRE scores are not required for this program.

International students are required to submit TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test scores.
Description: UMBC's Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) program is designed for early-to-mid-career professionals seeking a more foundational knowledge of GIS that goes beyond learning the basics of technology or application of analytical tools. As a GIS student, you will learn crucial GIS methods that connect global thinking with local action. You will also contribute to projects that address timely societal and environmental issues with a “place-based” dimension. [4] This Master of Professional Studies (MPS) in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is a 10-course/30 credit applied science program designed for students seeking either professional or academic careers. [2] The program is specifically for those interested in establishing their GIS credentials that rests on systematic critical thinking as it applies to social and environmental disciplines. [2] Each class, whether analytical or technical, employs scientific methods to assess problems by formulating plans and creating processes to produce well-thought-out and reasoned solutions in cartographic production, programming, dynamic visualization, data management, and spatial analysis. [2] Students will also gain an understanding of essential geographic principles and concepts needed to solve problems in nearly any industry or academic discipline. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Health Information Technology
Description: The Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Health Information Technology is designed to prepare computer science, information systems, and healthcare professionals to fill a range of new and expanding roles in the healthcare industry. The ten-course Health IT degree combines courses in Health Information Technology strategy, policy, and management with more technical, hands-on Health Information Technology courses that allow students to develop a formal educational program that best meets their individual career development needs. The program’s blend of practical management and technically focused courses prepares students for a range of opportunities within the growing healthcare technology profession.

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Industrial-Organizational Psychology
Requirements:
Admission Requirements

Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in any undergraduate major from a regionally accredited institution.

Have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. For students with an undergraduate GPA between 2.5 and 2.99, an option for provisional admission may be available for the fall semester only. This requires an in-person interview, and a decision will be made by the program director.

Submission of the following documents:
A completed application.
Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions.
A resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
A personal statement of academic and professional goals.
Three letters of recommendation.

The GRE is not required for admission to this program.

International applicants are required to provide TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores. Please refer to the Graduate School’s website for more information on English proficiency requirements.
Department: Department of Psychology
Description: UMBC's master's program in I-O Psychology, offered through the Department of Psychology, emphasizes key topics such as organizational behavioral management, consulting, human factors, and human resources practice. [4] Students engage in hands-on training while developing a professional portfolio and building relationships with faculty and industry professionals. [4] This program prepares graduates for diverse careers in Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, Organizational Behavior, and Training and Development. [4] It is offered in-person at the Shady Grove location in Rockville, MD, with flexible scheduling options for working professionals. [4] The M.P.S. degree in I/O Psychology is a 30-credit master's level program with credits distributed among core courses (15 credits), elective courses (12 credits), and a capstone course (3 credits). [3] Students will gain advanced knowledge in competencies including: Statistical Methods and Data Analysis, Ethical, Legal and Professional Contexts, Measurements of Individual Differences, Criterion Development, Job and Task Analysis, Employee Selection, Placement and Classification, Performance Appraisal and Feedback, Work Motivation, and Organizational Development. [3]
ScholarshipType: UMBC participates in all federal and state student financial aid programs and offers scholarships and assistantships through the Graduate School, Graduate Departments and the Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Software Engineering
Requirements: B.S. degree with a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale; Introductory programming courses completed in the last 10 years with a grade 'B' or above (see note below); Official Transcripts; Goal statement outlining the student's goals and expectations in the program; Resume or CV. [1]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology, Division of Professional Studies
Description: UMBC's Master of Professional Studies in Software Engineering provides the advanced knowledge, skills, and experiences to successfully build software intensive products not only for today's market but for tomorrow. [2] After successfully completing the program, you will be ready to take on the role of building a modern software intensive product, architecting a new solution, leading a team of engineers and product team to develop a new application, advise a government agency on how to make software contribute to the nation's growth, or venture on your own and create a new startup for a new software intensive product to make money and meaning. [2] There is no limit to what you can accomplish with the advanced skills and experiences gained from emerging software engineering techniques to software testing, verification, and validation, to building software that is ethical, reliable, and beautiful and how to engineer software for AI and with AI. [2] In partnership with UMBC's Division of Professional Studies, this program is designed to fit a busy schedule for working professionals interested in learning from industry professionals. [1] Additionally, students will gain exposure to coursework in leadership, communications, management, and ethics. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Technical Management
Requirements: Applying to the Graduate School at UMBC requires the submission of several documents. General requirements include transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, a goal statement or statement of purpose, and letters of reference. [6] The Graduate School recommends a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. [2] Specific programs may have additional requirements, such as a resume/CV, writing sample, or standardized test scores. [6]
Department: Master of Professional Studies
Description:
UMBC’s Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Technical Management is designed for experienced professionals who wish to develop the skills necessary to lead and manage technical teams, projects, and organizations. The program focuses on providing a solid foundation in management principles while also addressing the unique challenges of a technology-driven workplace.

The curriculum is built around a core set of six courses that provide the foundational knowledge in leadership, communications, ethics, and project management. The core courses are supplemented with technically oriented courses in entrepreneurship, international project management, and organizational leadership. Students can earn certificates in systems engineering, and cybersecurity along with the Masters degree.

The core curriculum can be augmented by a student’s choosing one of the following pathways or developing an individual program of study with the approval of the graduate program director. The following pathways are recommended for students who wish to focus their studies in a particular technical area:

Quality Management
Logistics/Supply Chain Management
Project Management
Systems Engineering

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants should have a bachelor's degree from an accredited university with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0. The program normally requires a bachelor's degree in mathematics or applied mathematics. Candidates whose degree is in another field (for example, computer science, physics, or engineering) and whose background in mathematics is strong are also eligible for admission. A combined verbal and quantitative GRE examination score of at least 304 and an analytic writing score of at least 2.5 are required. [1] TOEFL scores (if required) should be a minimum of 80/550 (internet-based/paper-based test scores). [1] Two letters of recommendation are required. [1]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: UMBC's master's degree in applied mathematics provides training in applications of mathematics that prepare students for employment in industry or government agencies. The master's degree can also serve as a bridge between undergraduate work and a doctoral program. [2, 5] There are two options: A course-based program culminates in a written comprehensive exam, and a thesis-based option culminates in completion of a research thesis. [5]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Molecular Biology
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants to the M.S. in Applied Molecular Biology program are required to submit a statement of purpose and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description:
The Master of Science in Applied Molecular Biology is designed to give the student a thorough grounding in the theory and practice of molecular biology. The hallmark of the program is a two-semester, seven-credit laboratory course that teaches students the state-of-the-art techniques of molecular biology in the context of an independent research project. In addition, the students take four lecture courses and prepare a scholarly paper on their research project. The program not only prepares its graduates to become middle-level researchers in the biotechnology industry, but it also provides excellent training for students intending to enter a Ph.D. program after graduation.

An accelerated master’s program is available to UMBC undergraduate students majoring in biological sciences. It allows our students to begin work on the M.S. in Applied Molecular Biology while completing the B.S. degree. This allows the students to complete the B.S. degree and the M.S. degree in four or five years.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Applicants to the Biological Sciences M.S. program should have a baccalaureate degree in a science or engineering discipline from an accredited university or college, a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale and should submit a statement of purpose describing their interest in the program and career goals and three letters of recommendation from persons in a position to judge the applicant’s academic abilities and potential for graduate study.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Concentration.1: ['Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (BMB)', 'Cell Biology and Developmental Biology (CMB)', 'Computational Biology and Bioinformatics (CBB)', 'Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (EEB)', 'Microbiology and Immunology (MI)', 'Neurobiology (NEUR)', 'Translational and Mechanistic Biology (TMB)']
Description: The graduate program in Biological Sciences is a research-oriented program in which students receive training in a modern, broad-based curriculum that emphasizes the development of critical and creative thinking. The course of study leads to the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees. All students are initially admitted into one of two departments within the College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences, the Department of Biological Sciences or the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry. There is a single, unified graduate curriculum for all students in the Biological Sciences graduate program that provides the students with the flexibility to receive training and to conduct research in any of seven programs of study (called tracks). The program is particularly well-suited for students with interdisciplinary research interests. The Biological Sciences graduate program also offers a non-thesis M.S. degree option.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical and Biochemical Engineering
Requirements: Applicants may have undergraduate degrees in engineering, or other disciplines. All applicants are expected to have completed the necessary prerequisites to begin the core curriculum for the degree program of interest. Requirements include: Unofficial transcript(s) with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale), required prior coursework, and two (2) or more letters of recommendation from professional or academic references. For International students, English Language proficiency scores are required. [3]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, applicants to the M.S. and Ph.D. programs in chemistry or biochemistry are expected to have a bachelor’s degree in chemistry or biochemistry with a minimum GPA of 3.0. This degree must include coursework in organic chemistry, physical chemistry and calculus. It is expected that applicants will have taken the Graduate Record Examination (GRE), but this is not a requirement for admission. Three letters of recommendation and a statement of purpose are also required.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The M.S. degree in chemistry is offered with a thesis and a non-thesis option. For the thesis option, the student must complete 30 credit hours of course work (including the core program), including six credit hours of CHEM 799: Master’s Thesis Research. The non-thesis M.S. degree requires 30 credit hours of course work (including the core program), including three credit hours of CHEM 600: Advanced Laboratory Projects. For both options, 18 credits must be at the 600-level or higher. A final oral examination is required for both options. Upon entry into the program, each M.S. student will be assigned an academic advisor from the graduate committee, who will assist the student in selecting a program of study. During the first year of graduate study, M.S. students who select the thesis option will consult with individual faculty members to select a research advisor and a research topic. Following selection of a research advisor, the student, in consultation with the research advisor, will choose a guidance committee. For thesis M.S. students, no later than the end of the second year of study, the student must submit a research proposal to the committee and successfully defend it in an oral examination.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, specific requirements for admission to the M.S. program in computer engineering are as follows: A B.S. degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field, such as computer science or physics. An undergraduate grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. International students must have a minimum TOEFL score of 80... In addition, all applicants must submit three letters of recommendation and a statement of purposes with their application.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
Description: The Master of Science in Computer Engineering program is designed to extend the knowledge of qualified students in the field of computer engineering. It provides a deeper and broader background in the traditional areas of computer engineering, as well as in the new and evolving areas of the discipline. The program consists of a set of core courses, a set of concentration areas, electives and a thesis or project research option. The M.S. degree may be completed on either a full-time or a part-time basis. The program provides a balance of theory and practical application to prepare students for careers in industry and for further graduate study.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
Concentration.1: ['Artificial Intelligence', 'Computer Science', 'Software Engineering']
Description: The department offers a graduate program leading to the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Computer Science. This program provides advanced instruction and training and research opportunities to prepare students for careers in industry, academia and government agencies. The program reflects state-of-the-art knowledge in major theoretical and applied aspects of computation. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Cybersecurity
Department: Graduate School

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, another engineering field, computer science, mathematics or physics. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is generally required.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Engineering Management
Requirements: Applicants must possess an accredited bachelor's degree in a science or engineering discipline, or the equivalent. During the application process, each applicant must select a specific technical track within the M.S. E.M. program. Students must possess sufficient prerequisite knowledge to enroll and succeed in the advanced technical courses for their proposed track (or willingness to enroll in any prerequisites for these courses). A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required. Three letters of recommendation are required. Satisfactory scores on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) are required. This requirement may be waived for applicants with significant work experience or a previously earned master’s or doctoral degree. International students must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: All degree-seeking applicants are required to submit an online application, pay a non-refundable application fee, and provide official transcripts from each college or university attended. A Statement of Purpose is also required for all degree-seeking applicants. Individual graduate programs may have additional requirements, such as letters of recommendation, portfolios, or standardized test scores.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
ScholarshipType: Graduate assistantships for teaching and research

ProgramName: Master of Science in Human-Centered Computing
Requirements: A bachelor's/undergraduate degree from an accredited university (3 year bachelor's degrees are accepted). An undergraduate GPA above 3.2. All applicants are expected to read, speak, write, and understand the English language fluently. GREs are not required for the MS Program. Statement of Purpose. [1]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Information Systems
Requirements:
In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, the M.S. in IS program requires:

- A bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field, with a minimum GPA of 3.0.

- Students with a non-IS/CS/CE bachelor’s degree are required to complete a set of foundation courses with a grade of “B” or better before they are admitted to the M.S. in IS program. In exceptional cases, work experience can be substituted for the foundation courses. Students who complete the IS undergraduate certificate program at UMBC can also satisfy this requirement.

- The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission to the program.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Master of Science in Marine, Estuarine & Environmental Sciences
Requirements: Statement describing applicant's interests in environmental sciences and reason for pursuing a MEES degree; specific course requirements depending on area of specialization; identification of mentor must be resolved as part of application process. [1]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering

The graduate may find employment in government and industrial laboratories, advanced technology firms or teach in community colleges. The Master's Degree program has a thesis and a non-thesis option. See the Mechanical Engineering website (me.umbc.edu) for complete program requirements. [8]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
ScholarshipType: Research and teaching assistantships and scholarships

Requirements: In addition to the Graduate School’s requirements, the Physics M.S. program requires a Bachelor’s degree in physics or a closely related field. A statement of purpose is required. Letters of recommendation are also required. The GRE is not required for admission.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Systems Engineering
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Systems Engineering is an interdisciplinary program that prepares engineers and other technical professionals for a career in the analysis, design, and management of complex systems over their life cycles. The program focuses on the development and application of systems-level thinking to a variety of engineering challenges. It offers advanced study in a variety of subjects, including systems architecture and design, system modeling and simulation, and project management, and it covers all phases of the system life cycle, from concept development to disposal.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants should have a solid background in mathematics and/or statistics. International students whose native language is not English are required to have a TOEFL score of >600 (paper), >250 (computer), or >100 (iBT). [2]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics requires 48 credit hours of coursework and research beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are also required to pass a comprehensive examination, a qualifying examination on a research topic, and to write and defend a dissertation containing original research. Research in the department is currently conducted in the areas of analysis, control theory, dynamical systems, game theory, numerical analysis, optimization, partial differential equations, probability, and statistics. Further details about the graduate programs in mathematics and statistics may be found on the department’s website, www.math.umbc.edu.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Atmospheric Physics
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, which are summarized in the Admissions section of this catalog, the following are the minimal requirements for admission to the Ph.D. program in Atmospheric Physics: A bachelor of science degree in physics, meteorology or a closely related field, such as chemistry, engineering or mathematics. An undergraduate grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Satisfactory scores on the verbal, quantitative and analytical-writing portions of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Three letters of recommendation from persons familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional background. A statement of purpose (academic goals). For those students whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 550 (paper-based), 213 (computer-based) or 80 (internet-based) is required.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in Atmospheric Physics is designed to provide students with a strong background in the physical and chemical processes that govern the atmosphere, and to train them in the methods of atmospheric research. In addition to the required courses listed below, Ph.D. students must take at least one specialized graduate course in a sub-field of their dissertation research, which must be approved by the Graduate Program Director. The final course requirements for a Ph.D. student are determined by the student's dissertation committee. A minimum of 18 credit hours of dissertation research (PHYS 899) is required for the Ph.D. degree.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biochemistry
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, applicants for admission to the Ph.D. program in biochemistry are expected to have a strong background in chemistry, including courses in calculus, physics, physical chemistry, organic chemistry, and biochemistry. Deficiencies in any of these areas can be made up during the first year of graduate study, but this may increase the time needed to complete the degree. Three letters of recommendation are required, as well as a statement of the student’s academic and professional goals. The GRE is not a required component of the application for admission. Students who have already earned a master’s degree may petition to have up to six credits applied to the PhD degree requirements. International students must also submit TOEFL scores.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Applicants are holistically evaluated according to their undergraduate coursework, their grade point average score (GPA), their graduate record examination score (GRE), their letters of recommendation, written statement of goals and interests, and background and experience. Applicants may have undergraduate degrees from biological, computational, or other disciplines. However, applicants are expected to have scholarly competence in biology, computer science, or/and mathematics. To be admitted to graduate study in the Department of Biological Sciences, students should have the following recommended preparation: Calculus (one semester); Organic Chemistry (two semesters with laboratory); Physics (two semesters); Genetics (one semester); Cell Biology (one semester); Research Experience (preferred, but not required). [5]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

Description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree in Biological Sciences is a research-based degree that prepares students for careers as professional biologists in academia, government and industry. The program emphasizes the development of critical thinking and independent research. Each student’s program is planned in consultation with the student’s mentor and advisory committee, with the dissertation research project as the central focus. Students must successfully complete a minimum of 40 credit hours of coursework, a qualifying examination, and a final thesis defense. Coursework includes core courses in the student’s track and specialized courses chosen by the student in consultation with his or her advisory committee.

For international applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum score of 80 on the TOEFL test, or 6.5 on the IELTS test.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: The application process for the CSEE Ph.D. program requires the Graduate School Application Form, a “Statement of Academic Goals and Research Interests/Statement of Purpose", official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, and three letters of recommendation. [9] Applicants should have a B.S. degree from an ABET-accredited undergraduate program in electrical engineering, or a strong academic record in computer science, mathematics, physics, or other areas of engineering or science. [7] The GRE General Test is required, but there is an option to waive it. [7]
Department: The Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering is a degree with emphasis on research. It provides for students who wish to increase knowledge in many areas of electrical engineering.
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering (Ph.D. in EE) is a research-oriented degree for students with a master’s degree in electrical engineering or a closely related field, such as computer engineering or physics. The program is designed to provide specialization in a number of research areas, and to develop the student’s ability to do independent creative work. The areas of specialization are broadly categorized as communications and signal processing and microelectronics and photonics.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Gerontology
Requirements: All applicants must submit an online application, pay the application fee, and submit official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Other required supporting documents include a statement of purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae, and three letters of recommendation. The GRE General Test is not required for admission.
Description: The PhD program in Gerontology is an intercampus, interdisciplinary research degree program at UMBC and the University of Maryland School of Medicine at the University of Maryland, Baltimore. You'll build on the complex, dynamic, and bi-directional relationships among individuals and the historical, political, economic, environmental, psychological, social, cultural and biological contexts in which aging occurs. [4] The program provides an interdisciplinary and integrative perspective on the process of human aging and the experiences of growing old. [3] The goal of the program is to train a new generation of gerontology scholars conversant with interdisciplinary and integrative paradigms and research designs employed to examine the unique, reciprocal, and dynamic nature of aging in context. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Human-Centered Computing
Requirements: Applicants must submit a statement of purpose. Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a CV demonstrating their past research, education, and employment accomplishments. Applicants must submit three letters of recommendation. The GRE is optional for the program. All applicants are expected to read, speak, write, and understand the English language fluently. Those whose native language is not English are required to take the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS), unless they have earned a post-secondary degree from an accredited university in the United States.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Human Services Psychology
Requirements: Admission to the program is based on a holistic review of applicants' materials. Applicants are expected to write a personal statement. In the statement, applicants should make sure to indicate how their: 1) interests align with the faculty mentor(s) they have identified and 2) interests, experiences, and/or future goals align with the HSP program's commitment to diversity, inclusion, and social justice. Applicants who do not have a degree in Psychology should explicitly specify their preparation and foundational knowledge necessary for admission into a doctoral program in Psychology. Three letters of recommendation are required from professors or professionals that can speak to your professional experience or educational background. Unofficial transcripts can be used for admission considerations, however you will be required to submit official transcripts if you are admitted. Applicants may identify up to two faculty members who will serve as their faculty mentor.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Concentration.1: The Human Services Psychology program at UMBC offers concentrations in Clinical Psychology, Behavioral Medicine, and Community Psychology. [1]
Description: The Human Services Psychology program is composed of three interrelated and complementary programs which provide education and training in clinical psychology, behavioral medicine, and community psychology. Initiated in 1983, the Human Services Psychology Program represents a reconceptualization of clinical psychology and several related specialties. Human Services Psychology is defined as that sector of professional psychology concerned with the promotion of human well-being through the acquisition and application of psychological knowledge and principles concerned with the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of psychological and physical disorders. The program is based on a scientist-practitioner model of training which aims to provide students with skills as both researchers and practitioners. It uses a biopsychosocial approach as the integrative perspective for its training. [1]
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA). [6]

Applicants should have a strong academic record and show an aptitude for research. It is expected that applicants have a Master's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related area. In some cases, a student may be admitted with a Bachelor's degree, with the expectation that the student will complete the requirements for a Master's of Science in Information Systems degree before being advanced to Ph.D. candidacy.

Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are optional. TOEFL scores are required for international students whose native language is not English. Three letters of recommendation are required. A statement of purpose is required, detailing the student's research interests and career goals. A resume or curriculum vitae is also required.
Department: Information Systems Department

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Language, Literacy, and Culture
Requirements: Admission to the LLC doctoral program is highly competitive. At a minimum all applicants must have a master's degree and meet all of the admissions requirements as set forth by the Graduate School. In addition, applicants must submit an academic writing sample with their application. [9] A 3.0 GPA or above on a 4.0 scale is required. [2] The program deadline for receipt of all application materials is January 15 of the calendar year in which the student intends to enroll. [9]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The interdisciplinary doctoral program in Language, Literacy, and Culture investigates the concepts and processes of language, literacy, and culture in relationship to social, cultural, linguistic, historical, technological, and ideological formations. [10] This interdisciplinary program draws upon the departments of Africana Studies; American Studies; Education; English; Gender, Women's + Sexuality Studies; History; Media and Communication Studies; Modern Languages, Linguistics and Intercultural Communication; and Sociology, Anthropology, and Public Health at UMBC. [10]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Marine, Estuarine & Environmental Sciences
Requirements:
In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, the MEES Program requires:

*   For Ph.D. applicants, a preferred minimum GPA of 3.0.

Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required. All application materials must be submitted online through the Graduate School’s website.

Description: Marine Estuarine Environmental Sciences (MEES) is an inter-institutional graduate program of the University System of Maryland whose mission is to educate students to become the scientific leaders and problem-solvers of the future. Using an interdisciplinary approach, we train students to engage in scientific discovery, integration, and application to generate new knowledge and to solve environmental problems. [8] The Marine Estuarine Environmental Sciences (MEES) graduate program is a highly interdisciplinary, multi-campus graduate program in marine and environmental science. [5, 6] The program's strength is drawn from the diverse expertise of its faculty affiliated with several USM institutions, as well as from government and non-government agencies. [5, 6] The program affords students an unparalleled opportunity to combine the expertise of the best environmental scientists in the region to guide their program of study. [5, 6] While the interests of students in the program are diverse, they generally center on some aspect of the interaction between biological, physical and/or chemical systems in the environment. [4, 5] Research activities range from studies of molecular mechanisms to fisheries ecology, chemical pollutants, or economics of environmental impact. [5]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: The basic admission requirement is a Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Civil, or Chemical Engineering. [4] A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.3 on a 4.0 scale is required for the Ph.D. program. [2, 4] Students with backgrounds in other fields like Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or Chemistry may be admitted but might need to complete prerequisite courses. [4] Applicants for the Ph.D. program must submit 3 letters of recommendation. [4]
Description: The PhD in Mechanical Engineering will prepare graduates for industrial and/or academic research as well as for higher-level jobs in mechanical-related industry. The design and manufacturing of power plants, automobiles, aircrafts, helmets, robots, and the development of new materials and systems for improved methods of transportation, energy and production by industrial robots are but a few important inventions that would not have been realized without the creativity associated with the mechanical engineering profession. The mechanical engineering academic program provides a well-balanced curriculum in the following areas of specialization: mechanical systems, mechanics, robotics and mechatronics, thermo/fluid systems, heating- ventilation-and-air-conditioning (HVAC), material characterization, manufacturing and automation systems, materials science and engineering, multidisciplinary design optimization and inverse design, computational analysis and distributed parallel computing, biomechanics, laser and plasma materials processing, nanomaterials, nanotechnology, electronic packaging, optical measurement and diagnostics, waste management, and renewable energy. This program provides an opportunity for students to enhance their technical knowledge and to conduct advanced research that can aid in their professional development and pursuit of research-related employment in the mechanical engineering field.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Molecular and Cell Biology
Requirements: Degree requirements: Background in calculus, general physics, organic chemistry, biochemistry and general biology, including genetics. Students intending to do research in computational biology should have some background in mathematics and in programming. Entering students not having this background may be required to take some additional course work in their first year or in the summer immediately preceding entry. [2] Applicants are holistically evaluated according to their undergraduate coursework, their grade point average score (GPA), their graduate record examination score (GRE), their letters of recommendation, written statement of goals and interests, and background and experience. Description: The Ph.D. program in Molecular and Cell Biology (MOCB) combines the substantial faculty resources and research facilities of several departments of the College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences and the College of Engineering at UMBC to offer an interdisciplinary, state-of-the-art educational experience for those desiring advanced training in molecular and cell biology. The program provides participants with the conceptual and technical background to investigate basic or applied problems at the molecular and cellular levels, in the life, biomedical, and bioengineering sciences. The intent of the MOCB program is to provide an intensive, innovative but broadly-based training in molecular and cell biology.

Description: UMBC's Ph.D. in physics offers excellent training in disciplines such as astrophysics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics and quantum information science. Opportunities abound for interactions with faculty and students in disciplines outside the department, such as electrical and mechanical engineering and physical chemistry. Graduates frequently continue on to postdoctoral fellowships in academia, high-tech jobs in private industry, or roles in government labs or agencies such as NASA and NIST. UMBC has strong links to NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in nearby Greenbelt, MD. The UMBC physics department offers a wealth of opportunities while still being small enough to promote a close-knit, collegial environment, including an active Physics Graduate Student Association.

Each program’s section of the graduate catalog contains a statement of the program’s specific requirements. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the skills to conduct original research, critically evaluate scholarly literature, and effectively apply statistical computing tools.

[1] This program is designed for three types of students: Students looking to strengthen their skills before applying to graduate music programs. [1] Students who wish to focus their music study on contemporary music. [1] Ensembles seeking an intense program that not only hones musical skills but focuses on developing a complete entrepreneurial package to prepare for professional life. [1]

The certificate if open to student with a bachelor's degree in any undergraduate major. Courses may be applied to the Master of Arts program in Applied Sociology if admitted.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Biochemical Regulatory Engineering
Requirements: The Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Biochemical Regulatory Engineering is a four-course (12 credit) program. To earn the certificate, students must complete BTEC 660, BTEC 662, BTEC 664, and BTEC 666. All credits may be applied to the Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.): Biotechnology degree. [3]

Description: The Biochemical Regulatory Engineering Post-Baccalaureate Certificate guides students through the ins and outs of the FDA process and explores the numerous considerations that can help ensure product approval and sustainable regulatory compliance status. Professionals from leading bioscience companies and government agency organizations participate in this program. The FDA must be involved at every step of product development, so knowing the internal framework of the FDA review and marketing authorization process can be a significant advantage for your career growth. UMBC’s post-baccalaureate program in biochemical regulatory engineering bridges the gap between your technical expertise and business knowledge of biochemical product development. Students in this program also gain insight from guest lecturers from the private and public sectors who have direct hands-on experience with various biotechnology topics.

The courses are taught by industry professionals with extensive practical experience in the subjects they teach.
