ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Cybersecurity Operations
Requirements: There are no specific constraints on the type of undergraduate degree required for this certificate. In general, applicants should understand the basic concepts and operation of the Internet, networked information systems, and have a basic familiarity with information security concepts and/or practices. Those with a background in computer science or information systems, or with significant professional experience in the IT industry are encouraged to apply. A 3.0 GPA or above on a 4.0 scale is required. [1]
Description: This four-course post-baccalaureate certificate is oriented towards students seeking broad exposure to cybersecurity principles, best practices, and technologies, and can be completed in a year. This certificate includes three required cybersecurity courses and one student-selected exploratory elective on a cybersecurity topic of interest or professional relevance. If a student is accepted into the M.S.: Cybersecurity, all four certificate courses count toward that degree.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Cybersecurity Strategy & Policy
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree is required for admission to the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Cybersecurity Strategy & Policy program. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is recommended, but work experience or other factors may be considered in place of the GPA recommendation.
Description: In the Cybersecurity Strategy and Policy certificate program, students will learn how to analyze cybersecurity risks, develop appropriate protection & response options, and assess operational requirements for government, military, critical infrastructure, and commercial missions. [3] This four-course graduate certificate is oriented towards students seeking broad exposure to cybersecurity principles and how they relate to national or global cybersecurity, and can be completed in a year. [4] Because these courses are not significantly technical, this program is available to students with a variety of undergraduate backgrounds. [4] Students may choose to take this certificate by itself, or they may take this certificate and then later complete the master's. [4] If a student is accepted into the M.S.: Cybersecurity, all four certificate courses count toward that degree. [4]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Data Science
Requirements: A bachelor's degree is required to apply. [12] Applicants should have a GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale. [12] Additionally, candidates are expected to have completed post-secondary education in calculus, statistics, and basic programming. [12] Official transcripts from every college and university attended must be submitted. [12]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
Description: The Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Data Science provides a graduate-level, 12-credit sequence of courses for students with a bachelor’s degree to develop a strong foundation in the field. Students will acquire a deep understanding of core data science concepts and will be trained in the use of a variety of data-analysis tools. The certificate program aims to provide students with the necessary skills to be competitive for data-science-related jobs and to succeed in a data-science-related career in a variety of fields.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Dementia Care Services
Requirements: In addition to the Graduate School’s requirements, the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Dementia Care Services requires the following: A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. A statement of goals for pursuing this certificate. A current resume. One letter of recommendation is preferred.
Department: The Erickson School
Description: Grow in understanding of dementia while incorporating the implications for individuals, families, care providers, practice and policy, and society. Upon certificate completion, you should be able to develop a multi and interdisciplinary understanding of dementia and approaches to dementia care and identify current and innovative models of care and support for those living with dementia.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Digital Forensics
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline. Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Basic understanding of the internet, networked information systems and information security.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in eLearning
Requirements:
Application Requirements:

- A completed University of Maryland Graduate School application.
- A statement of goals, highlighting the applicant’s career goals and how the certificate program will help them achieve their goals.
- A current resume.
- A writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to write in a professional and/or academic context.
- Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions.
- For more information on how to apply, go to isd.umbc.edu.
Department: The Graduate School, Learning and Performance Technology
Description: UMass Boston’s Instructional Design for E-Learning Certificate is a 4-course, 12-credit graduate certificate program that prepares you for a career in the growing field of instructional design and technology in business, industry, and education. You will acquire the skills and dispositions to pursue or advance your career as a member of an instructional design team or as a training and development specialist. All four courses will count toward the Instructional Design MEd program.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Emergency Management
Requirements: UMBC offers the option for baccalaureate degree holders to take a limited number of graduate courses in a narrowly defined area of special interest in order to expand their educational preparation, and, in some cases, to prepare the student for professional certification examinations. Prospective students who wish to take the certificate program only should apply via online application. Please make sure you are applying for the correct program and modality.
Department: Department of Emergency Health Services
Description: The Department of Emergency Health Services (EHS) offers a Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Emergency Management. It is intended to help current and aspiring emergency managers to develop graduate-level analytical, planning, and leadership skills in the increasingly important field of all-hazards emergency management, with a series of courses that are also designed to provide the educational material needed to qualify students for the certification exam of the International Association of Emergency Managers.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Engineering Management
Requirements: Applicants must have a B.S. degree in engineering, computer science or a related technical field. A 3.0 undergraduate GPA is required for admission. In addition, applicants should have a year of college-level calculus, a semester of probability and statistics, and a semester of engineering economy. Students who do not have these prerequisites may be admitted provisionally and will be required to complete them before or during their first two semesters in the program.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology, Division of Professional Studies
Description: The engineering management post-baccalaureate certificate program is designed to help you complement your existing disciplinary expertise with new business skills. This program is designed for engineers employed in technology-oriented enterprises or government programs. All of the courses in the certificate program can be applied to the master of science in engineering management.
MaxFails: Students may apply no more than six semester hours of work with a grade of C or C+ toward graduation. [1]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Entrepreneurship
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree with a GPA of 3.0 or better, or be a current UMBC graduate student in good standing with a GPA of 3.0 or better.
Description: This certificate has an emphasis on building an entrepreneurial mindset in sales and marketing. It is intended for someone starting a new company or social enterprise. Students will learn the tools necessary to apply entrepreneurial thinking in their work and life. Students will learn the creative solving problem process, which helps them torecognize opportunities for improving performance, choose correctly from a wide variety of resources for solving problems efficiently, anticipate problems in project planning, and promote the continuous involvement of others. [2] Students will learn the basic fundamentals of sales, review the relationship of customer need identification, and discuss reasons that make people buy. [2] Students will learn the basic six steps of selling and discuss the real world marketing challenges involved in launching an entrepreneurship venture or sustaining competitive advantage. Students will learn how to create a competitive analysis, prepare a customer analysis, determine target market and positioning, understand pricing management, and develop marketing objectives and goals. [2]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Geographic Information Systems
Requirements: A bachelor's degree and 3.0 GPA (Students with a GPA less than 3.0 may be admitted to the Certificate program); Statement outlining the student's goals and expectations in the program; Current resume; Two Letters of Recommendation (MPS only; Optional for Certificate); Official transcript(s) from each college & university attended; GRE is not required; English proficiency testing (TOEFL/ IELTS) is required for international students. [2]
Description: The post-baccalaureate certificate in Geographic Information Systems applies critical GIS toward improving the lives of people, society, and the environment. Students will gain an understanding of essential geographic principles and concepts needed to solve problems in nearly any industry or academic discipline. Completing the certificate instills a foundation of spatial knowledge and technical skills for careers that employ spatial computing. Students are able to earn this certificate first and then choose to transfer all of the credits into a Master’s of Professional Studies in Geographic Information Systems.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Innovation
Requirements: Applicants for the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Innovation must possess a bachelor's degree in any subject and are generally expected to have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. [2, 7] In addition to meeting the Graduate School's general requirements, applicants are required to submit a one-page statement of purpose that outlines their interest in the program and how it will support their career goals.
Department: The Graduate School
Description: The Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Innovation is designed to help you become a leader in innovation by thinking and acting in new and different ways. Participants will learn how to lead collaborative teams to apply design thinking and other structured processes to create breakthrough solutions. Through hands-on experience, you'll practice evidence-based decision-making and learn to foster a culture of innovation that promotes calculated risk-taking and learning from failure. The program culminates in a real-world innovation challenge, where you will apply what you've learned to address a challenge from your own organization or a community partner.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Instructional Systems Development
Requirements: The general application for degree-seeking students at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) may require several documents, although not all may be necessary for every program. Applicants should verify the specific requirements for their desired program. Commonly required or requested documents include a goal statement, contact information for references, education history, and transcripts. [4] Unofficial transcripts can often be used for initial admission consideration, but official transcripts are required upon admission. [4]
Department: Division of Professional Studies
Description: The Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Instructional Systems Development is for individuals who wish to enter the field of training and development, and for those who are already in the field and want to update their skills. The required courses provide a strong foundation in adult learning, instructional systems development and training principles. The elective courses provide a range of opportunities for students to focus on specific areas of interest.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Instructional Technology
Requirements: As of Fall 2024, applications are currently not being accepted for the Instructional Technology certificate program. [1, 3]
Department: Division of Professional Studies
Description: The four-course (12-credit) Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Instructional Technology provides current and aspiring instructional designers, corporate trainers, and P-20 educators with the knowledge and skills to effectively use technology for teaching and learning in a variety of contexts. The certificate curriculum will enable those who complete the program to analyze learning needs; locate, evaluate, and create digital resources; design and assess effective learning experiences; and model ethical and legal best practices. The certificate also provides a foundation for students who may later decide to continue on to a master's program in the field.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Integrated Product Development and Manufacturing
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in a technical background, marketing, industrial design and similar disciplines. Applicants should have an overall grade point average of 3.0 or higher on a 4-point grading scale in the B.S. course work and any previous graduate courses. [1]
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology, Division of Professional Studies
Description: Gain a deep understanding of the challenges and opportunities of current manufacturing processes in a program designed for working professionals to quickly upgrade their skills. The environment around product development and manufacturing is complex and ever-changing. The certificate program in Integrated Product Development and Manufacturing covers the organizational, logistic, and technical requirements of current manufacturing processes and methods. The program provides hands-on experience with a selection of fabrication tools to allow you to understand the manufacturing process inside and out.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Leadership
Requirements:
A bachelor’s degree.
A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Submission of the online application, including residency information.
Submission of official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions.
A current, professional resume.
A personal statement of one to three pages that explains how this certificate will help the applicant in his/her career.
Department: The Erickson School of Aging, Management, and Policy
Description: The Organizational Leadership Certificate provides advanced education and training in organizational leadership of human service and nonprofit programs to direct practice social work students and members of the community. [1]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Learning and Performance Technology
Requirements: Applying to the Graduate School at UMBC requires information regarding your academic history, professional background, and personal information. [3] An unofficial transcript from your bachelor's degree granting institution must be part of your application package. [3] Students who are unable to meet the minimum GPA standards may still be admitted to graduate study by demonstrating outstanding performance on one or more of the graduate aptitude tests or by providing strong letters of recommendation. [2] For first-year undergraduate students, an essay is required, which helps the admissions team get to know you. [5]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Mechatronics
Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a closely related field. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. For students with a non-engineering B.S. degree, a grade of “B” or better in the following UMBC (or equivalent) courses is required: MATH 152, PHYS 121 and CMPE 212 or CMSC 202.
Department: The College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Organizational Consulting
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree with a minimum 3.0 GPA.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: UMBC’s Graduate Certificate in Organizational Consulting prepares professionals to excel as both internal and external consultants, addressing human performance and organizational challenges. This program covers essential functions and skills needed to diagnose and solve complex issues within organizations. Students will learn integrated approaches to implementing large-scale changes through coursework that includes case studies and experiential learning opportunities. The program offers a practical, hands-on experience via a structured internship, where students are mentored by seasoned consultants in real consulting environments. With a curriculum developed in partnership between UMBC’s Industrial/Organizational Psychology and Learning and Performance Technology programs, the certificate provides a comprehensive perspective on consulting practices.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Project Management
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
Description: The Project Management program at UMBC is designed to provide professionals with the skills and critical analysis capabilities necessary to successfully complete projects, lead technical, virtual, and international teams. Students will demonstrate a knowledge of project management practices as outlined by the Project Management Institute (PMI). This certificate is ideal for professionals in a variety of industries. It emphasizes practical skills that are directly applicable and complementary to courses offered through other applied professional programs.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Systems Engineering
Requirements:
In addition to the Graduate School’s general admission requirements, the Systems Engineering graduate program requires the following for admission to the certificate program:

A bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, mathematics, or a related technical field.
A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology
ScholarshipType: Federal loans, Federal Work-Study, assistantships, and some scholarships. [3]

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Requirements: Applicants to the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in TESOL must complete a graduate application. Applicants should have earned a bachelor’s degree with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. A two-page goal statement is also required.
Department: Department of Education
MaxFails: A cumulative GPA of 3.0 must be maintained to remain in good academic standing. No grade below C will be accepted for graduate credit.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in The Non Profit Sector
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: This certificate is designed for college graduates who wish to understand the role of the nonprofit sector in our society. It will provide an understanding of nonprofit organizations based on systematically examining relationships with the private sector and government. The certificate is open to students with a bachelor’s degree in any undergraduate major.

ProgramName: Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Training and Talent Development
Requirements: Applicants should have a GPA of 3.0 or above. Additionally, they are expected to have completed Introduction to Psychology OR General Psychology, along with one undergraduate course in Research Methods or Statistics. [1]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: UMBC’s Training and Talent Development Certificate is crafted for early to mid-career HR professionals who aspire to deepen their expertise in performance improvement and training methodologies. This program covers essential principles such as the role of training within organizations, adult learning theories, needs assessment, and training evaluation. Students will develop practical skills in designing and managing training programs, navigating through the Instructional Systems Design (ISD) process to create projects ready for implementation. Additionally, the curriculum provides insights into both the historical and modern perspectives of leadership, equipping students with the tools to support and enhance organizational performance. The 12-credit program consists of four courses, and the credits earned can be applied towards a Master’s degree in I/O Psychology or Learning and Performance Technology, offering a flexible pathway for professional advancement.

ProgramName: Concentration in Economic Policy
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School, applicants for admission to the M.A. in E.P.A. should have a bachelor’s degree from a recognized university, with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Applicants must also have successfully completed at least one semester of statistics and at least one semester of calculus. Students who do not meet these course pre-requisites may be admitted on a provisional basis, but must complete them with a grade of “B” or better before being fully admitted to the program.
Concentration.1: Economic Policy
Description: For students who would like to focus on the economic tools used in policy analysis. This is the broadest and most flexible concentration.

ProgramName: Concentration in Public Policy
Requirements: Applicants must have or be nearing completion of a bachelor's degree to apply to the Master's program. For the Ph.D. program, applicants often have a master's degree, but it is not required. [2] The application requires the submission of official transcripts from all universities attended, a statement of goals, and contact information for at least three recommenders. [2]
Department: School of Public Policy
Concentration.1: Public Policy
Description: The public policy major has one concentration: public policy. It prepares students for a variety of careers and for several types of graduate or professional training. The program is designed to develop the analytical skills needed to understand the basis for public policy, the process of its creation and the assessment of its consequences. To this end, the curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing on a variety of social science disciplines. Students acquire a set of skills and a broad background in policy studies. The program provides the foundations needed for students who wish to pursue graduate work in public policy or in one of the social sciences. The B.A. program provides the background for professional training in such fields as law, social work and public administration. The program also provides the skills and knowledge needed by those who wish to work immediately after graduation in the public or non-profit sectors.

ProgramName: Concentration in Economic Policy and Data Sciences
Requirements: In addition to the general requirements of the Graduate School, applicants for admission to the M.A. in Economic and Data Sciences must have a bachelor’s degree, a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, submission of a statement of purpose, submission of a resume, and submission of three letters of recommendation. Submission of Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores is optional.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Concentration.1: Economic Policy and Data Sciences
Description: The concentration in Economic Policy and Data Sciences provides students with advanced training in data science with a focus on applying these techniques to economic and policy issues. Students are required to demonstrate proficiency in a number of data science techniques as well as the ability to apply these techniques to a new research question in their capstone project. The capstone project must be approved by a committee of three faculty members and is the primary requirement for the concentration.

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Bayesian analysis
Requirements: This area of emphasis is available to students in the Ph.D. and M.S. programs in Statistics. Admission Requirements: Admission to the Statistics M.S. or Ph.D. program.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Concentration.1: Area of Emphasis in Bayesian analysis
Description: The Area of Emphasis in Bayesian Analysis provides M.S. and Ph.D. students with a solid foundation in the concepts of Bayesian statistical analysis. This area of emphasis is available to students in the Statistics M.S. and Ph.D. programs. The emphasis is designed to be taken as part of the degree program. The requirements for the area of emphasis involve 9 credit hours of course work, of which 3 credits may be counted towards the degree requirements in the Statistics M.S. and Ph.D. programs.

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Biostatistics
Department: The College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Concentration.1: Biostatistics Track
Description: Applications-oriented tracks are offered under the master’s program in statistics to meet the educational needs of students who intend to obtain employment in industry and government. The program offers a track in environmental statistics and a track in biostatistics. This track is recommended for students interested in biomedical and public health applications. The program is a joint undertaking of the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at UMBC and the Department of Epidemiology and Preventive Medicine at the University of Maryland, Baltimore.

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Data mining
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Design of experiments
Requirements: The 'Area of Emphasis in Design of Experiments' is a track within the Bachelor of Science in Statistics, not a separate program to which one directly applies. Application is for general undergraduate admission to UMBC. Requirements include completing the Common App, an essay, and submitting high school transcripts. There is a $75 non-refundable application fee. [6]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Fees: For the 2024-2025 academic year, the estimated undergraduate tuition and fees are $13,256 for Maryland residents and $31,225 for out-of-state students. [4]
Fees.1: For the 2024-2025 academic year, the estimated undergraduate tuition and fees are $13,256 for Maryland residents and $31,225 for out-of-state students. [4]
Concentration.1: Applied Mathematics / Statistics Track
Description: The applied track focuses on mathematics as it is used in the sciences and engineering, and in industry. Students should consult with their advisors before selecting a track.
Accredidation: UMBC is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education, 3624 Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104. (267-284-5000). MSCHE is an institutional accrediting agency recognized by the U.S. Secretary of Education and the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA).
CostPerCredit: UMBC charges $389 per credit hour for in-state undergraduates and $1,136 for out-of-state undergraduates. [4]

[3]

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Environmental statistics
Requirements: The Area of Emphasis in Environmental Statistics is part of the Statistics M.S. and Ph.D. programs. Applicants to the program must have a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university. Applicants must submit an application to the Graduate School. The application should include a transcript or transcripts of all academic work, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose and a resume. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required. International students must also provide a TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic, or Duolingo score.
Department: Department of Mathematics and Statistics

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Nonparametric statistics
Requirements: Applying to the Graduate School at UMBC requires information regarding your academic history, professional background, and personal information. Degree applications may require several reference materials, in addition to optional supplemental documents. Applicants should check their specific program's admission requirements as they may vary. [2]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Reliability
Requirements: An area of emphasis in Reliability requires the completion of 12 credits (4 courses).
Department: College of Engineering and Information Technology

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Spatial statistics and image analysis
Requirements: Criteria for admission include: A bachelor's degree with a grade point average higher than 3.0 out of 4.0. A sound background in mathematics and/or statistics. A GRE score in the 85th percentile in the quantitative section. A TOEFL score of at least 600 (paper-based test) or 250 (computer-based test) or 100 (iBT) for international students. [15]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Statistical decision theory and inference
Requirements: The completed application packet must include: (a) completed application forms; (b) transcripts of college and university academic records; (c) three recommendation letters; (d) Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores for the General Test; and (e) TOEFL score for international applicants whose native language is not English. Criteria for admission include: A bachelor's degree with a grade point average higher than 3.0 out of 4.0. A sound background in mathematics and/or statistics. A GRE score in the 85th percentile in the quantitative section. A TOEFL score of at least 600 (paper-based test) or 250 (computer-based test) or 100 (iBT) for international students. [10]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Concentration.1: Area of Emphasis in Statistical decision theory and inference
Description: The Department of Mathematics and Statistics offers graduate programs leading to the M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in both applied mathematics and statistics. Doctoral students continue with advanced study and dissertation research, with specialization in any of the departmental fields or in an interdisciplinary area. Particular emphasis is given to the following areas in statistics: Bayesian analysis, biostatistics, data mining, design of experiments, environmental statistics, nonparametric statistics, reliability, spatial statistics and image analysis, statistical decision theory and inference, survival analysis, time series analysis. [2, 3]

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Survival analysis
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Concentration.1: Area of Emphasis in Survival analysis
Description:
This area of emphasis is available for students in the Ph.D. and M.S. programs in Statistics.

Survival analysis is a cornerstone of modern biostatistics and has a wide range of applications in many other areas, including the social sciences, economics, and engineering. The basic data in survival analysis is the survival time, which is the time from a well-defined origin until the occurrence of a well-defined event. An important feature of survival data is the presence of censoring, which occurs when the event is not observed for some subjects. The Department of Mathematics and Statistics at UMBC has a strong group of faculty in survival analysis and related areas. This area of emphasis is designed for students who are interested in developing expertise in this important area of statistics.

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Time series analysis
Requirements: The provided URL is for an 'Area of Emphasis' and does not list application requirements. Application requirements for the overarching graduate programs in Statistics would apply. These generally include a bachelor's degree with substantial quantitative coursework and a minimum GPA.
Department: Department of Mathematics and Statistics
Concentration.1: Area of Emphasis in Time-Series Analysis
Description: The Department of Mathematics and Statistics offers an Area of Emphasis in Time-Series Analysis for students in the Statistics M.S. and Statistics Ph.D. programs. Students not in the Statistics M.S. or Ph.D. programs may be admitted with permission of the Graduate Program Director. This Area of Emphasis will prepare students for careers in fields in which time-series analysis is a key component, such as econometrics, engineering, finance, and signal processing. The emphasis will consist of four courses, as described below.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Bachelor's of Science (B.S.) in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (under the auspices of the Biological Sciences and the Chemistry and Biochemistry departments) offers students a unique interdisciplinary curriculum and exposure to a wide range of faculty members. [1] With a curriculum drawing from both disciplines, as well as specific biochemistry courses, the program provides a broad background in the physical and life sciences. [1] It is suitable for students planning careers in laboratory research or further training in graduate, medical, or other biomedical professional programs, such as medicine, dentistry, and medical technology. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology
Requirements: Application requirements for undergraduate programs at UMBC are generally not specified on a per-program basis. The provided program page lists detailed course and credit requirements for completing the degree, including 25 credits in Biology, 13 in Chemistry, 17 in Computer Sciences, and 19 in Physics & Mathematics. [18] Specific admission documents like a resume or statement of purpose are not mentioned for this bachelor's program.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences, College of Engineering and Information Technology
Description: Get comprehensive training in the fields of bioinformatics and computational biology by combining courses in the areas of biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, and mathematics. [3] Bioinformatics and Computational Biology is one of the fastest growing fields in the country. As a Bioinformatics and Computational Biology student, you will develop skills across several disciplines and gain the knowledge that allows you to access and manipulate the wealth of data now emerging from new technologies relating to genes, genomes, and the molecules they produce. [3] A degree in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology will give you an excellent background for a job in industry, government, and academics, including future graduate study. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biological Sciences
Requirements: For first-year admission, applicants must submit the Common Application, a $75 non-refundable application fee, and an official high school transcript. An essay is also required to help the admissions committee get to know the applicant. [19, 21] Letters of recommendation are optional but up to two can be submitted through the Common App. [21]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The curriculum leading to the Biological Sciences, B.A. sweatshirts designed for students who want to pursue a career in a health-related profession (dentistry, medicine, pharmacy, or veterinary medicine) or those interested in training in an allied health field (dental hygiene, medical and research technology, nursing, pharmacy, or physical therapy). The B.A. is also appropriate for students wanting to combine another area of study - such as business, environmental studies, law, or science writing - with a solid background in biology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences
Requirements: For freshman admission to UMBC, a holistic review is conducted, considering grade point average, academic trend, strength of curriculum, a personal statement/essay, and optional letters of recommendation and standardized test scores. [3, 9] Specific course prerequisites for the Biological Sciences B.S. include biology, chemistry, physics, and calculus. [15, 17] A minimum grade of 'C' is required in all major courses and their prerequisites. [15, 19] Additionally, at least six of the eleven required Biological Sciences courses must be completed in residence at UMBC. [19]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in biological sciences is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in biology, while allowing them the flexibility to pursue their own specific interests. The B.S. degree requires a research experience and more in-depth study in a specific area of biology. Graduates from this program go on to professional schools (medical, dental, etc.), graduate programs in the biological sciences, and to a wide range of jobs in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries as well as at government agencies.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Field-Specific, Identity-based, Community service, Military-affiliated, Employer-sponsored, Micro-scholarships. [3, 16, 18, 20, 24]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biology Education
Requirements: To apply, first-year students need to complete the Common App. Required supporting documents include an official high school transcript. Submission of standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) and letters of recommendation is optional. [11, 19] A personal statement or essay is required. [14]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: The B.A. program in biology education is designed for students who want to teach biology in a secondary school setting. The curriculum meets the requirements for a bachelor's degree in biological sciences and also provides the education courses needed for teacher certification. Students completing this degree will have a strong foundation in the biological sciences and educational pedagogy that will allow them to find employment as secondary education biology teachers or in a range of other technical positions utilizing their STEM education.
Accredidation: UMBC's Education Department has been nationally reaccredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Education Preparation (CAEP) from 2020 to 2027. The Secondary Science (Biology) program was included in the CAEP accreditation review. All programs offered by the UMBC Department of Education have also been approved by the Maryland State Department of Education. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry Education
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry Education, you must complete the Common App. You will also be required to submit your official transcript. You may choose to submit standardized test scores and/or letters of recommendation. [12]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: Offered by Chemistry and Biochemistry, the Chemistry Education, B.A. provides a curriculum that gives students a solid foundation in chemistry and the coursework necessary for certification to teach chemistry at the secondary level. [3] It is considered crucial that graduates be fully trained chemists, capable of working in a range of technical positions outside of secondary education. [3] The curriculum also seeks to expand the scientific background/perspective of graduates by requiring courses in other scientific disciplines as well as a science history course. [3]
Accredidation: The chemistry program is certified by the American Chemical Society. The education component of the B.A. in Chemistry Education is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The mathematics component of the Bachelor of Arts program surveys the classical areas of mathematics—analysis, algebra and geometry—and their history. Courses in statistics and in computer science provide a taste of two relatively young branches of the mathematical sciences. The B.A. degree provides a strong background in mathematics and is especially appropriate for students who intend to pursue careers in such fields as secondary education, law, business or medicine. The B.A. requirements are more flexible than those for the B.S. For instance, there is a modern language requirement and a related course requirement specifically designed to accommodate subject matter outside the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. To examine the remarkable variety of possibilities, see the requirements for the B.A. listed below.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: The application requirements for freshman applicants include the Common Application, an official high school transcript, and an essay/personal statement (submitted as part of the Common Application). [0, 2] A letter of recommendation is recommended but not required. [0]
Concentration: ['Specialty toward Graduate Studies', 'Specialty in Applied Mathematics', 'Specialty in Optimization and Operations Research', 'Specialty in Actuarial Science', 'Specialty in Statistical Sciences', 'Specialty in Mathematics Education']
Description: This major is designed to give students a broad perspective on various fields of mathematics, especially areas closely associated with applications, such as mathematical modeling, differential equations, numerical algorithms, and statistical analysis. [5] Within the major, you can pursue a few specialties: graduate studies, applied mathematics, optimization and operations research, actuarial science, statistical sciences, or mathematics education. [5] You can choose from either a Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science (B.S.); the B.S. includes additional core courses in mathematical analysis and physics as well as additional electives and supplementary requirements. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics Education
Requirements: General application requirements for graduate programs are not specified at the institute level; applicants are directed to the individual program of study to determine the specific materials required. For undergraduates, UMBC has a test-optional policy regarding SAT and ACT scores.
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: Students enrolled in the Physics Education, B.A. satisfy requirements in physics, education and those needed for teacher certification. Students in this program work closely with advisors in both Physics and Education when choosing courses. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: General requirements for graduate admission include a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited university and a minimum GPA of 3.0, though some programs may have higher requirements. [2] For undergraduate admission, requirements include submission of an application, an official high school transcript, a list of senior year courses, an essay, and a non-refundable application fee. [1] The submission of standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) is optional for most undergraduate applicants. [1, 4]
Concentration: ['Professional Track', 'Secondary Education Certification Track', 'Applied Physics Track']
Description: The B.S. in Physics is a rigorous program that prepares students for graduate studies in physics and other physical sciences, or for a wide variety of careers in industry, technology, and government labs. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the fundamental areas of physics, including mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermal physics, and quantum mechanics. Students also have the opportunity to take advanced courses in specialized areas such as astrophysics, condensed matter physics, and optics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Description:
The Program in Statistics

Statistics is the science and art of making inferences from data under conditions of uncertainty. The practice of statistics requires not only an understanding of statistical techniques, but also some understanding of the nuances of the problem requiring statistical analysis - whether it is in the social or physical sciences, engineering, medicine or business.

The major program leading to a B.S. in Statistics, offered by the Department of Mathematics and Statistics, is geared toward the above goal. The educational program is designed to give students a broad perspective on the theory and applications of statistics. In particular, the interdisciplinary curriculum structure of the program helps develop skills in the application of statistical methods to a variety of disciplines. The university’s state-of-the-art computing facilities are available to all students and are used in conjunction with instruction. UMBC is the only institution in Maryland offering an undergraduate major in statistics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Translational Life Science Technology
Requirements: To apply, prospective students must complete the Common App, which includes a personal essay. [2] Applicants are also required to submit an official high school transcript. [4] International students may have additional requirements, such as credential evaluations for transcripts from outside the U.S. [2, 4]
Department: College of Natural and Mathematical Sciences
Description: UMBC's Bachelor of Science in Translational Life Science Technology is a unique degree designed to help you claim your future in the competitive biotechnology industry. [1] This degree program combines the theory of a traditional life science degree with hands-on, real-world applications of the process for turning scientific discoveries into real life-saving solutions. [1] When you complete your degree, you will have a comprehensive understanding of science, mathematics, engineering, and lab-based research as they apply to the design and development of diagnostics, therapeutics, vaccines, and other biotechnology products answering current and emerging health and environment risks. [1] Students in the Bioinformatics track will also receive extensive training in computer systems, bioinformatics, machine learning and artificial intelligence. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting
Requirements: Admission to the B.F.A. in Acting is by audition, usually at the end of the freshman year. All students who wish to pursue the B.F.A. must first be accepted into the B.A. program in theatre. B.F.A. acting candidates are expected to demonstrate commitment to the program through participation in productions and in all appropriate classes. At the audition, the student will be expected to perform a prepared audition piece and to demonstrate, through an interview, a commitment to the profession and to the training. A 3.0 GPA in theatre courses is also required for admission to the B.F.A. track. In addition to departmental admission, students must meet all university general education and graduation requirements.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships for in-state students may be in the amount of $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000 per academic year. For out-of-state students, the amounts are $10,000, $15,000, or $22,000 per academic year. [3, 5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies, you need to complete the Common App. Required supporting documents include your official transcript and an international transcript if applicable. Applicants may also choose to submit standardized test scores and/or letters of recommendation. [14]
Description:
The Department of Africana Studies (AFST) provides students of all ethnic, national, and cultural backgrounds the necessary tools to understand, critically evaluate, analyze, and interpret events and phenomena that structure the experiences, possibilities and dynamics of the people of African descent in the United States, Africa and its diasporas. [2] AFST students are offered a broad array of courses addressing cultural, economic, historical, political, psychological, and sociological issues that affect peoples of African descent from diverse disciplinary and comparative perspectives. [2]

Africana Studies at UMBC offers a rigorous and challenging academic program that prepares students to think and write critically and clearly, engage in research and service, argue persuasively, and effectively solve problems. [2] Africana Studies adopts an interdisciplinary approach that is sensitive to the interests and outlook of the people of African descent and their contributions to the interdependent global world through teaching, research, and service in human development and civilization, arts and the sciences. [2] Students may pursue the standard major in Africana studies or a concentration in community involvement studies. [2] Many students find it productive to combine Africana studies with another discipline in a dual major. [2] Students also may minor in Africana studies. [2] Students who select the major or double-major in Africana Studies have the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge through internships or field research. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students include completing the Common App, paying a $75 non-refundable application fee, submitting an official high school transcript, and writing an essay. [4, 9] Letters of recommendation are listed as optional. [4] International students may have additional requirements, such as credential evaluations for post-secondary work outside the U.S. [4]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: American Studies is an interdisciplinary field in which we analyze various facets of American culture with a focus on issues of race, ethnicity, class, and gender. The Department of American Studies is the oldest interdisciplinary department on campus. We are a leader on campus in fields of community-engaged research and public humanities. [14] The Department of American Studies provides students with the skills to critically analyze issues of race, place, and identity through a local and transnational lens. [14] In American Studies we use an array of methods to study diverse subject areas including: multiethnic literatures and the diverse ways people read and interpret texts, the political economic and ethnographic dimensions of food, place-based approaches to urban development, and histories of policing and prisons. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Ancient Studies, applicants must complete the Common App. Required supporting documents include an official transcript and an international transcript if applicable. Applicants may also choose to submit standardized test scores and/or letters of recommendation. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies requires the completion of 39 credits. These credits are distributed among core courses (12 credits), concentration courses (12 credits), and language courses (15 credits). Students must choose one of three concentrations: China and Japan, Asia and Globalization, or Asia and Business. The language requirement involves completing three semesters of an approved Asian language (Chinese, Japanese, or Korean) or demonstrating equivalent proficiency.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies combines work in anthropology, art history, geography, history, language, literature, political science, and/or religious studies. Majors select one of five concentrations: China, the Islamic World, Japan, South and Southeast Asia, or the general Asian Studies option with no specific geographic focus. Courses for this program are offered by several departments: Anthropology, Art, Geography, History, Political Science, Religious Studies, and World Languages and Cultures, a​as well as occasional special topics courses in other areas.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cultural Anthropology
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The B.A. Track in Cultural Anthropology focuses on the issues, modes of inquiry, fieldwork strategies, methods of data selection and analysis, and forms of ethnographic representation that characterize contemporary cultural anthropology. The Cultural Anthropology Track is intended for students interested in current cultural, social, and political issues, especially in understanding the relationship of global processes to new cultural forms and social inequalities. [1] Students learn how cultural theory is integrated with empirical ethnographic research and how to balance knowledge of worldwide interconnections with in-depth knowledge of particular geographic regions (e.g., Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the United States). [1] Students trained in Cultural Anthropology develop a unique set of skills enabling them to work successfully in many different cultural environments; a major in Cultural Anthropology also provides excellent preparation for students planning graduate training in anthropology or other disciplines, including professional training in law, teaching, and social work. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Dance
Requirements: Admission to the B.A. in dance is contingent on the successful completion of a dance audition.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The B.A. in dance offers a program of study in the creative, historical, cultural, and scientific aspects of dance as a performing art. The program prepares students for graduate studies and professional careers as performers, choreographers, teachers, and scholars. Majors may select from three concentrations: dance education, dance performance and choreography, or dance studies.
Accredidation: The dance program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD). The Dance Education concentration is accredited by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Design
Requirements: Admission to the B.F.A. in design is a two-step process. The first is acceptance to UMBC. The second is a portfolio review for acceptance into the B.F.A. program. Applicants must submit a portfolio of 15-20 pieces of their work and a brief essay that addresses their interest in the field of design.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The B.F.A. in Design is an 82-credit, pre-professional course of study with focused tracks in graphic design, animation and intermedia. The curriculum is designed to broaden and expand a student’s formal and conceptual vocabulary in creative design practices, while introducing them to new ways of thinking about images, time, space and audience. Students gain skills necessary to visually communicate ideas. Aspiring designers are invited to join our internationally renowned program that focuses on addressing complex questions in visual communication. Students graduate with a strong set of critical-thinking and creative skills, setting them up for future success in the media and design industries.
Accredidation: The B.F.A. is an accredited program of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: General admission to the Graduate School at UMBC requires an undergraduate degree from a regionally accredited institution or a comparable degree from a recognized foreign institution. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is typically required, though some programs may have higher standards. Individual graduate programs often have their own specific requirements for admission, which may include a statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, and a resume or portfolio.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Economics requires 13 courses, of which 9 are in economics, 2 in mathematics and 2 in statistics. The B.A. prepares students for a wide range of career opportunities in business, government and the non-profit sector. Our graduates have found employment in finance, banking, insurance, marketing and sales. They also work as analysts and statisticians for federal and state government agencies. The B.A. also provides a sound basis for the professional study of law, business and public policy. Students who are considering graduate study in economics should pursue a B.S. in Economics.
MinGPA: A grade of “C” or better is required in each course to fulfill major requirements.
ScholarshipType: UMBC offers a range of financial aid options, including grants, scholarships, work-study, and loans. Students can use the Scholarship Retriever tool to find institutional and departmental scholarships.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Emergency and Disaster Health Systems
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Emergency and Disaster Health Systems is concurrent with the general admission requirements for first-year students at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). Applicants must apply through the Common Application.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Paramedic Concentration', 'Emergency Health Leadership Track', 'Emergency and Disaster Health Management Track']
Description: Earning a bachelor's degree in Emergency and Disaster Health Systems at UMBC equips you with the knowledge and skills to lead and respond effectively in critical health and safety roles. [2] This program prepares you to make a lasting impact in your community by combining practical training with leadership development. [2] The BS in Emergency and Disaster Health Systems provides a comprehensive education for a wide range of students. [2] Whether you are beginning your journey to become a certified paramedic, returning to complete your bachelor degree in emergency management to advance your career, or seeking specialized training in disaster management, you will gain the expertise to succeed. [2] The curriculum emphasizes both applied skills and professional growth, ensuring graduates are ready for impactful careers across emergency response and public safety. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: To apply for admission to UMBC as a first-year student, the following is required: completion of the Application for Undergraduate Admissions (the Common App), a $75 non-refundable application fee, and an official copy of the student's current high school transcript. An essay is also required as part of the application. [12, 16]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Concentration: ['Communication and Technology', 'Creative Writing', 'Literature', 'Language, Media, and Culture']
Description: The B.A. in English offers students a choice of four tracks: Literature, Creative Writing, Communication & Technology, and Language, Media, and Culture. The Literature track provides a comprehensive overview of British, American and World literatures, with a strong emphasis on the development of students’ skills in writing and textual analysis. The Creative Writing track offers a range of workshops in the genres of fiction, poetry, and creative nonfiction. In these workshops, students learn the elements of craft and a variety of techniques as they develop their own creative work. The Communication and Technology track offers courses in written and spoken communication, with a particular emphasis on the critical analysis of media and technology. The Language, Media, and Culture track studies the ways in which language, in and of itself, and as it is employed in a wide array of media, shapes and gives meaning to our world and our experiences. English courses at the 100 and 200 level are designed to help all UMBC students from a wide variety of majors improve their skills in writing, speaking, and critical analysis. At the 300 and 400 level, the curriculum offers majors and other interested students a broad range of courses in language, literature, and culture, rhetoric and composition, creative writing, and communications. The department prides itself on its innovative teaching and on the close contact between faculty and students. The English Department is also home to the university’s new interdisciplinary minor in Public Humanities, which encourages students to think about ways in which the skills of the humanities may be used to address real-world problems and engage a variety of publics. The English Honors Program offers students the opportunity to undertake an extended research or creative project in close consultation with a faculty mentor. The department also offers an accelerated B.A./M.A. that allows qualified undergraduates to begin taking graduate courses in our M.A. in Texts, Technology, and Literature.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science and Geography
Requirements: To apply, first-year students must complete the Common App. Required supporting documents include an official high school transcript. Applicants may also choose to submit standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) and/or letters of recommendation, though these are optional. [7]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The B.S. in Environmental Science and Geography is a rigorous, interdisciplinary degree that prepares students for a variety of careers by providing a solid foundation in the physical and natural sciences, coupled with training in geospatial technologies. Coursework from the Geography and Environmental Systems department is combined with courses from chemistry, physics, biology and mathematics. The B.S. degree has two tracks: one in environmental science and one in geography. The environmental science track focuses on understanding how physical and natural systems function, how humans are impacting those systems and what interventions are required to maintain more sustainable systems. This track is designed for students interested in careers such as hydrology, water quality, environmental restoration, and conservation science. The physical geography track has similar requirements but is designed for students who are more interested in understanding physical processes on the Earth’s surface, such as fluvial, hillslope, and coastal processes. This track prepares students for careers in fields such as earth science, geomorphology, and watershed management. Both tracks prepare students for graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Financial Economics
Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Financial Economics consists of at least 60 credits distributed as described below. A grade of “C” or better is required in each course to fulfill major requirements. Students must take a minimum of 21 credits from UMBC (not transferred) ECON courses. Students may complete a maximum of one major or minor from Economics.
MaxFails: A student may not have a third attempt for ECON 311, ECON 312, and ECON 374. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender, Women's, and Sexuality Studies
Requirements: For prospective first-year students, application for admission to UMBC consists of the following: Completion of the Application for Undergraduate Admissions (Common App), a $75 non-refundable application fee, an official copy of the student's current high school transcript, and a required essay. [7, 12] Submitting official SAT or ACT scores is optional, as are two letters of recommendation. [12]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: Gender, Women’s, + Sexuality Studies is an interdisciplinary field of inquiry that investigates how gender and sexuality operate as organizing axes of social, cultural, aconomoc and political institutions, as well as in the everyday lives and cultural products of people who must live within them. Emphasizing the importance of historical and cross-cultural and transnational perspectives, Gender, Women’s, + Sexuality Studies at UMBC critically examines the intersections of gender and sexuality with other differences, including, class, race, ethnicity, nationality, age, and ability to make visible structures of power that otherwise remain hidden. We empower students to imagine a more just future and equip them with the tools to collectively enact it.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography and Environmental Studies
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies
Requirements: For first-year admission, applicants must submit the Common Application, a $75 non-refundable application fee, and an official high school transcript. An essay is a required part of the application. [4, 8] The admissions review is holistic, considering grade point average, academic trend, and strength of curriculum. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Jazz Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Jazz Studies, prospective students must complete the Common App. [9] Applicants are required to submit their official transcript. [9] For visual and performing arts majors, there may be additional requirements and deadlines specific to the program. [9] An audition is also a required part of the application process for admission to the program.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Media and Communication Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the media and communication studies major, students must have completed at least 28 academic credits and have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.50. Additionally, students must have completed MCS 101: Introduction to Media and Communication Studies and MCS 222: Communication and Media Theory with a grade of "C" or better.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description:
The Media and Communication Studies curriculum provides a comprehensive understanding of the media and communication industries and their social impact. The program is designed to develop students’ abilities to think critically and to communicate effectively. In addition, the program provides analytical and professional skills that prepare students for careers as communication professionals and for graduate study. 

The program’s academic requirements comprise a 15-credit core sequence and 24 credits of electives. The 100- and 200-level core courses must be completed before students can enroll in the 400-level core course, and the core courses must be completed before students can enroll in the capstone course. All courses in the major must be completed with a grade of “C” or better.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Middle Grades STEM
Requirements: To apply, you must complete the Common App. You will also be required to submit your official transcript. International transcripts must be submitted if applicable. [3]
Department: Department of Education

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Modern Languages and Linguistics
Requirements: Application requirements are not specific to the 'Bachelor of Arts in Modern Languages and Linguistics' program but are handled by the central UMBC Undergraduate Admissions. Applicants must submit the Common App, an application fee, and official high school transcripts. [4, 9] A personal essay is required as part of the Common App. [4]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The B.A. in Modern Languages and Linguistics provides students with a comprehensive knowledge of one or more modern languages (French, German, Russian, Spanish), as well as a deeper understanding of the nature of language, its structure, and its cultural embedding through the study of linguistics. The specific language concentrations (French, German, Russian and Spanish) provide students with a variety of courses in language, literature, culture and related fields (e.g., film studies, history, political science, and translation). The linguistics concentration provides students with a variety of courses in theoretical and applied linguistics (e.g. phonology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics and second language acquisition). All the programs of the Department of Modern Languages, Linguistics and Intercultural Communication share a common commitment to the value of intercultural communication and the development of intercultural competence. Students in all our programs are strongly encouraged to participate in a study-abroad program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Composition
Requirements: In addition to completing the Common App for university admission, there are additional requirements for Visual and Performing Arts majors. [8] The catalog states, 'In addition to a university application, a separate application to the Department of Music is required for all prospective music majors and minors. All entering students are required to audition and to take a music theory placement exam.'
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Performance
Requirements: In addition to meeting the university’s general admission requirements, all students intending to major in music must perform an entrance audition on their principal instrument or voice. On the basis of this audition, the department faculty determines a student’s readiness for the music major of his or her choice.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Teaching and Learning
Requirements: Admission to the music programs is by audition. Students should apply to the university through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions and Scholarships. [2] All students who wish to major or minor in music must audition for the Department of Music. [4]
Department: Department of Music

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Technology
Requirements: Admission to the B.A. in music technology requires an audition on a primary instrument or voice, as well as a portfolio review. In addition to meeting the university’s general admission requirements, students wishing to major in music must perform an audition on their primary instrument or voice for the music faculty and complete a theory and ear-training placement examination.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students at UMBC include submission of the Common Application, an official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, and an essay. There are no additional, program-specific requirements mentioned for the Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year admission include: Completion of the Application for Undergraduate Admissions (Common App), a $75 non-refundable application fee, an official copy of the student's current high school transcript, and a required essay. [8, 9] Submission of official SAT or ACT scores and up to two letters of recommendation are optional. [8, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: UMBC's review of applicants for undergraduate admission considers a number of factors. These include grade point average, academic trend, strength of curriculum, personal statement/essay, optional letters of recommendation, and other achievements. [6, 16] Submitting official SAT or ACT scores is optional for first-year applicants. [11]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Description: The psychology major is designed to provide a basic core of courses that will acquaint students with the various sub-fields of psychology and the methodology of the discipline. For some, the undergraduate major will be preparatory to graduate study in psychology. For others, it will be an important component of a liberal arts education that can be applied to a variety of careers. Most graduate programs in psychology (both M.A. and Ph.D.) require a bachelor's degree in psychology. It is sometimes required that B.A. students take additional research methods and life science-oriented courses to gain acceptance into Ph.D. programs that have a life science orientation. Students should consult with their advisors about the specific requirements for graduate programs in which they have an interest. Both the B.A. and B.S. are options for students interested in graduate school; the B.S. is not necessary for admission to most graduate programs in psychology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Requirements: The admissions committee at UMBC conducts a holistic review of each applicant, considering high school grade point average, the strength of the curriculum, class rank, and other achievements. [9] An essay is a required part of the application. [9] Applicants must submit an official high school transcript. [6] For students with fewer than 30 college credits, an official high school transcript is required. [9] Letters of recommendation are optional but will be reviewed. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Health
Requirements: General freshman application requirements include submission of the Common Application, an official high school transcript, and an essay. UMBC also requires a non-refundable application fee. A letter of recommendation is strongly recommended but not required.
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Public Health will prepare students to identify, understand and address public health problems at the local, state, national and global levels. The B.A. program requires courses in the social and behavioral sciences and humanities. The B.A. degree prepares students to enter the workforce as public health professionals or to continue their studies in graduate school in a variety of fields, including public health, health care administration and public policy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students at UMBC include the submission of an official high school transcript. [3] An essay is also a part of the application process. [3]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
ScholarshipType: The university offers institutional and departmental scholarships which can be explored via a 'Scholarship Retriever' tool. [27]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre
Requirements: For general admission, first-year students must submit an application and have an official high school transcript sent to the university. [6] A personal essay is also required to help the admissions office get to know the applicant. [7] An application fee of $75 is required. [6, 7] While not explicitly listed for the B.A. in Theatre, a holistic review for general undergraduate admission considers grade point average, academic trend, strength of curriculum, personal statement, letters of recommendation, and other achievements. [2]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences
Description:
The B.A. in Theatre provides a broad, liberal arts education in the history, theory and practice of theatre. The curriculum offers a comprehensive course of study that balances theory and performance, providing students a solid foundation as theatre artists, scholars and practitioners.

The Department of Theatre is committed to a curriculum that equally supports performance, production, research and arts administration, and views its production season as an essential component of the academic curriculum. The department offers students numerous performance and production opportunities working with faculty, guest artists and student directors. In addition to a full main-stage season, the department produces a series of student-directed one-act plays, a devised work and student-initiated projects. The department offers travel/study opportunities and is active in the Kennedy Center American College Theatre Festival.

The theatre major prepares students for further education at the graduate level or for entry-level theatre work. Courses are structured to teach and hone practical skills while challenging students to achieve creative and intellectual excellence.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts, prospective students must complete the Common App. [6] Applicants are required to submit their official transcript. [6] They may also choose to submit standardized test scores and/or letters of recommendation. [6] As a Visual Arts major, applicants must also fulfill additional requirements, which include submitting a portfolio to pass the Portfolio Process and receive the “visual arts milestone,” which is a pre-requisite for the majority of courses and official acceptance into the Visual Arts program. [2, 6]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
Concentration: The UMBC Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts offers several concentrations: Animation, Graphic Design, Photography and Cinema, Print and Intermedia Arts, and Visual and Media Arts.
Description: UMBC's B.A. in Visual Arts is designed to deepen the foundational skills and techniques of a student's creative practice. The program provides opportunities to explore art history, animation, cinematic arts, graphic design, photography, print media, and intermedia arts. Students study various media-art forms under the guidance of internationally acclaimed faculty. The degree allows for a focus on the study of art and design within a liberal arts context, which helps develop critical thinking skills for a career in the visual arts and design.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Art and Design, Commission on Accreditation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Visual Arts
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Visual Arts, you must complete the Common App. Required supporting documents include your official transcript. International transcripts are required if applicable. Applicants can optionally submit standardized test scores and/or letters of recommendation. Those applying as Visual and Performing Arts majors should research any additional requirements and deadlines specific to the program. [13]
Department: College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences
